metadata.case_name: CHIU SHING WAI v. FUNG PING TONG AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: Multiple laceration on the right upper limb and forehead
source: 1. Multiple laceration on the right upper limb and forehead;
the plaintiff was discovered to have quadriplegia.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of cervical spinal cord, unspecified

injuries.description: haematoma on right knee; fracture of the right patella
source: X-rays showed a fracture of the right patella
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the knee or lower leg

source: 3. tenderness and deformity of the left leg.
X-rays showed a fracture of the left tibia and fibula.

manifestations.description: At first he could not move his limbs at all but gradually improvement took place and he achieved a considerable degree of movement in both the arms and legs. He was taught to walk with a tripod frame and he can get out of bed himself, stand up, hold the frame with both hands, move the frame forwards and even take a step with each leg, moving 1' forwards with each combined manipulation. In the ward at Pok Oi he can walk the length of the ward (about 60') and he does this several times in the morning and afternoon

He can only raise his right arm slowly to shoulder level and he has only a trace of movement in the fingers and hand and the movement is useless for any delicate manoeuvre although he can use the arm to push the wheels of the wheel chair. He can raise the left arm to slightly above shoulder level, he can hold a bowl in the left hand or hold a spoon
possible mild deterioration in his control of urine and bowels

treatments_received: Admitted to Princess Margaret Hospital (10 September 1979)
Open reduction and internal fixation (11 September 1979)
Treatment for pneumonia and high fever (post-operative complication)
Transferred to Rehabilitation Centre at Kwun Tong for six months of intensive physiotherapy and rehabilitation
treatments_future: Residence in a Care and Attention Home (Kam Tin Home mentioned as example)
Nursing care two or three times a week for 2 or 3 hours (advised by Dr. Wedderburn)
Medical supervision once a quarter (opinion of Dr. Tse Chor Fat)

losses.description: This comprises injuries which leave the victim with very restricted mobility; plaintiff taught to walk with a tripod frame and can walk the length of the ward (about 60') only
He would require somebody to come in, clean the room, cook his food, do the marketing etc.; assistance required for personal care and supervision

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Requires help for domestic tasks: clean the room, cook his food, do the marketing
Because of the risks of infection and disease, his life is likely to be shortened by at least 30% and he is unlikely to live after the age of 70
